speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Health whether he can provide an update on (i) the pilot for Pre-Implantation Genetic Screening (PGS) and (ii) when PGS can be included as a mainstream healthcare service.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think this pilot has been going on for about seven years now.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I am just wondering when the study will finally come to an end.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Is there a specific number of patients which we need to go to this study before we can consider ending the study and nationalising PGS?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, could I also asked whether the MOH is looking into expanding this to the private sector as well, where the private assisted reproduction (AR) clinics can also be part of this study, so that we can finally reach that number of patients that we are hoping to?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: However, as you can see, over time, we have worked on trying to increase the numbers and there are enrolments.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And this is something that we are reviewing and we are looking into.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As a matter of principle, I also want to highlight that there exists an infinite number of tests and screens that are available for many different conditions, including this one.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, this is something we do need to take into consideration.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is not just an issue of cost.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is also an issue of the side effects and some negative detrimental effects that may come.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we do need to consider this and we need to take into account all these factors before we can decide to mainstream this.
